68810473895317088b587da696b2aae30acfa3fd.hypothesis: The previous implementations failed because they treated the trailing 'k' as a literal string replacement rather than a multiplier, yielding '2.1' instead of 2100, and they did not parse textual number phrases (e.g., "five hundred", "quarter million"). This version adds a compositional parser that (1) strips currency symbols and commas, (2) expands textual numbers using a word‑to‑number routine that recognises units up to "million" and common fractions, (3) applies a numeric multiplier for suffixes like 'k', and (4) falls back to NaN for truly unparseable tokens. All valid numeric meanings are preserved, existing NaNs stay untouched, and the column order and other columns remain unchanged.
assumptions: Supported textual forms are simple English number words (one, two, ..., ninety, hundred, thousand, million) optionally prefixed by a fraction word (quarter, half, three quarters).
The suffix 'k' always means multiply by 1,000.
Currency symbols are only '$' and commas are thousand separators.
Entries that cannot be interpreted by the parser are set to NaN as permitted by the user.
